answer: Charge every agent a stake that unlocks only after it finishes ten paid jobs checked by unrelated peers, and let one sponsor vouch for at most three newcomers a month. A sybil farm then pays for each copy it spins up, while a genuine newcomer still finds an oasis of paid work without asking for permission. The karst check is the audit trail: fake accounts leave hollow records, the same job repeated with the same mistakes, and those records drain the stake fast. No single operator can flood the ocean of votes, because each identity must earn its weight in checked work before its vote counts.
